descriptions.text: FutureSwap's position contract computes a trading fee in token units (abs(delta) * feeRateWad / 1e18) and forwards that token-denominated value into FeeManager.addFee(...), where the receiving system instead interprets the argument as a fee weight / basis-points / share value. Because of this unit mismatch, an attacker opening positions with carefully chosen deltaAsset/deltaStable could inject absurdly large "bps"/weight values into the fee accounting. The attacker (using an Aave flashloan of ~500k USDC.e) seeded several positions through helper contracts, then called changePosition() with a large negative stable delta (changePosition(0, -894_992.852305 USDC, 0)) to redeem an inflated balance, draining ~394.7k USDC.e and ~67.5 WETH from the victim's inventory. Root cause: the value passed between the position logic and the FeeManager carried inconsistent units and lacked range validation. Vulnerable code snippet: Attack Tx: https://skylens.certik.com/tx/arb/0xe1e6aa5332deaf0fa0a3584113c17bedc906148730cbbc73efae16306121687b Analysis: https://x.com/nn0b0dyyy/status/2009922304927731717

The FutureSwap protocol deployed on Arbitrum was exploited again via a reentrancy vulnerability, following its first attack four days ago, resulting in a loss of approximately $74,000. The attacker had previously abused the reentrancy function 0x5308fcb1 three days earlier to over-mint LP tokens, and after the cooldown period expired, redeemed the excess collateralized assets to realize profit.

On 10 January 2026, the FutureSwap perpetual exchange contract on Arbitrum was exploited via a collateral accounting logic flaw. The attacker used flash loans and coordinated helper contracts to inflate the protocol's withdrawable collateral, draining approximately $394,743 in USDC.e from the protocol's liquidity pool. The protocol's changePosition function allowed user collateral withdrawals based on a global stable balance that included both deposited collateral and proceeds from Uniswap V3 hedging swaps. This enabled a malicious user to withdraw far more than their collateral entitlement, leading to a substantial loss.
